The problem with the rule that was proposed by the Obama administration in the waters of the United States was the result of two Supreme Court decisions, the swank and the promise decision back. in the mid-2000s. And the court, hard and fun here, kind of made the water a little bit because they didn't define navigable. And of course, when the Clean Water Act was passed in 1972, they put the word in the navigable. And they said, navigable waters will be under a more jurisdiction of the Clean Water Act than the U.S. EPA. And that was to go after the polluters of the 1960s and go after them with severe fines and even jail time, so the Clean Water Act. But they didn't define navigable. Now, you know, navigable to most people can go down the river. That's, I would say, navigable, it can do. You know, where's the stop? The Supreme Court decision said, well, they didn't define it either. And they left it open for waters that maybe it could affect what most people think navigable waters.
